rule: Scholarly theory sources explain or delimit theory objects; they do not replace the existing claim ledgers that document concrete Film & TV cases.

sources.title: The Classical Hollywood Cinema: Film Style and Mode of Production to 1960
sources.source_location: Book-level film-style and mode-of-production framework used here for formal systems, continuity norms and historically bounded stylistic conventions rather than as a universal model of all cinema.

sources.title: Audio-Vision: Sound on Screen
sources.source_location: Book-level audiovisual theory of relations between heard and seen material, used to prevent sound from being treated as a detachable annotation of images or as direct evidence of audience effect.

sources.title: Narration in Film
sources.source_location: Existing narratology reference in the Film & TV claim ledger; used for distinctions among filmic narration, knowledge distribution and construction of fictional worlds.

sources.title: Transmedia Storytelling 101
sources.source_location: Existing MIT-linked transmedia reference in the seriality/adaptation ledger; used as a bounded framework for coordinated storyworld expansion across media rather than a label for every franchise extension.

sources.title: Pink-Slipped: What Happened to Women in the Silent Film Industries?
sources.source_location: Monograph used for recovery historiography, archival absence and gendered labor histories; it supports methodological recovery frames rather than assuming that absence from canonical histories means absence from production.

sources.title: Uplift Cinema: The Emergence of African American Film and the Possibility of Black Modernity
sources.source_location: Historical study used for counter-archive and recovery approaches to early Black film cultures, institutions and surviving traces without treating later canonical visibility as a neutral record of historical production.

sources.title: Introduction to Documentary, Third Edition
sources.source_location: Documentary-studies framework used for modes, voice, representation and the documentary claim on the historical world; modes remain analytical tendencies rather than truth guarantees or rigid boxes.

sources.title: New Documentary
sources.source_location: Documentary theory used for performativity, mediation and negotiated relations between filmmaker, subject and representation; it is paired with evidence-provenance and ethics claims rather than used to dissolve factual verification.

sources.title: Television: The Public Sphere and National Identity
sources.source_location: Existing Oxford University Press monograph in the society/politics ledger; used for public-sphere infrastructure, television institutions and national identity without equating broadcast reach with shared opinion.

sources.title: Waving the Flag: Constructing a National Cinema in Britain
sources.source_location: Existing scholarly national-cinema source; used to treat national cinema as an institutional, discursive and industrial construction rather than a transparent expression of a single national identity.

sources.title: Production Culture: Industrial Reflexivity and Critical Practice in Film and Television
sources.source_location: Production-culture framework used to analyse self-theorizing industrial practices, occupational cultures and reflexive production discourse while keeping promotional self-description distinct from independently verified working conditions.

sources.title: Production Studies, The Sequel! Cultural Studies of Global Media Industries
sources.source_location: Edited production-studies volume used for labor, collaboration, institutions and global production contexts; production roles and guild positions remain evidence about specific practices, not universal descriptions of every production system.

sources.title: The Cultural Industries
sources.source_location: Political-economy framework for cultural-industry organization, risk, ownership and labor; used to interpret institutional structures while market concentration, policy effects and audience outcomes still require empirical evidence.

sources.title: Netflix Nations: The Geography of Digital Distribution
sources.source_location: Digital-distribution framework used for territory, catalog availability, platform geography and uneven distribution; it does not turn one platform's catalog or interface into evidence for all audiovisual circulation.

sources.title: Audience Reception Research in a Post-broadcasting Digital Age
sources.source_location: Existing peer-reviewed methodological audience source; used for reception as situated meaning-making and for mixed-method adaptation to fragmented digital media contexts.

sources.title: How audiences form: theorising audiences through how they develop relationships with film
sources.source_location: Existing audience-theory article used to frame audience formation as a process of developing relations with film rather than treating an audience as a pre-existing homogeneous population.

sources.title: Pleasure, disaffection, “conversion” or rejection? The (limited) role of prefiguration in shaping audience engagement and response
sources.source_location: Existing pre/post audience study used to keep prefiguration and expectation as bounded explanatory variables rather than deterministic predictors of post-viewing response.

sources.title: Cities and Cinema, 2nd edition
sources.source_location: Existing academic monograph used for historical and theoretical relations between cinematic form and urban representation rather than as evidence about a city's actual social conditions.

sources.title: Cinematic Urbanism: A History of the Modern from Reel to Real
sources.source_location: Existing academic monograph used for reciprocal relations between cinema, urban modernity and the imagined city while location facts remain independently sourced.

sources.title: Atlas of Emotion: Journeys in Art, Architecture, and Film
sources.source_location: Existing academic monograph used for embodied, mobile and affective approaches to cinematic space; it supplies an interpretive hypothesis, not evidence that every viewer experiences place identically.

sources.title: Space and Place: The Perspective of Experience
sources.source_location: Existing human-geography monograph used to distinguish abstract space, experienced place and attachment; it is a neighboring theoretical lens and does not substitute for film-form analysis.

sources.title: Cult Cinema: An Introduction
sources.source_location: Existing academic monograph used to keep cult status as a contested relation among reception, circulation, aesthetics, history and community rather than an intrinsic property of a text.

sources.title: Collective Cultural Memory as a TV Guide: ‘Living’ History and Nostalgia on the Digital Television Platform
sources.source_location: Existing television-memory article used for relations among archive reuse, nostalgia, programming and digital platforms while collective memory remains an analytical construct requiring reception evidence for audience-level claims.
